title: Vendor Secure Development & Patching Addendum - Template
content:
Purpose:
This addendum sets minimum secure-development, dependency-management, and patching obligations for third-party vendors ("Vendor") that develop, maintain, or deliver software or services integrated with Redwood Inference ("Company"). It is designed to be attached to a Master Services Agreement or Supplier Agreement and establishes objective timelines, evidence requirements, and remediation expectations to reduce supply-chain risk and ensure timely mitigation of vulnerabilities.

Scope and Applicability:
- Applies to all software, libraries, container images, infrastructure-as-code, and CI/CD pipelines that Vendor delivers or operates and that integrate with Company production or customer-facing environments.
- Does not replace privacy/data processing obligations (see DPA) but complements them for operational security.
- Parties may agree to stricter controls in a schedule for high-risk integrations.

Key Definitions (selected):
- "Critical Vulnerability": vulnerability with CVSS v3.1 base score >= 9.0 or an exploit in the wild known to affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Company systems or customer data.
- "High Vulnerability": CVSS 7.0–8.9.
- "Fix/Remediation": code change, patch, configuration update, or compensating control that eliminates or materially reduces risk.

Vendor Obligations:
1) Secure Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Practices
   - Maintain a documented SDLC that includes threat modeling, secure design reviews for new features that handle Company data, and mandatory code review practices for all production changes.
   - Use automated static application security testing (SAST) in CI for pushed code and prevent merging of code with new critical findings unless mitigated or explained in an approved risk acceptance.
   - Perform dependency/software composition analysis (SCA) at least weekly and block builds that introduce libraries with known critical vulnerabilities.
   - Require developer training on secure coding annually and maintain records of completion for staff working on Company integrations.

2) Secrets and Key Management
   - Prohibit storing Company secrets in plaintext in source control. Enforce secrets scanning during CI and rotate any exposed credentials within 24 hours of detection.
   - Provide evidence of secret management tooling and a policy for ephemeral keys where applicable.

3) Build and Release Controls
   - CI/CD pipelines that produce artifacts for Company must be reproducible and signed. Build artifacts (image digests or package checksums) used in production must be recorded and shared on request.
   - Implement controls preventing direct modification of production artifacts without an auditable release process.

4) Vulnerability Discovery and Disclosure
   - Vendor must maintain an internal vulnerability triage process and a public or Company-accessible channel for coordinated disclosure.
   - Newly discovered Critical vulnerabilities that impact Company must be acknowledged by Vendor within 6 hours of initial triage and a remediation plan provided within 24 hours.
   - For High vulnerabilities, Vendor must provide an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours and a remediation plan within 72 hours.

5) Patching and Remediation SLAs (applicable when Vendor maintains or hosts components)
   - Critical: remediation deployed to affected production instances within 7 calendar days of availability of a fix, or sooner if exploit in the wild; if a vendor patch is unavailable, implement compensating controls within 48 hours.
   - High: remediation deployed within 30 calendar days.
   - Medium/Low: documented plan and prioritized backlog; remediation timelines to be agreed quarterly.
   - Exceptions require written approval from Company Security and must include compensating controls and monitoring until remediated.

6) Penetration Testing and SCA Evidence
   - For any vendor-hosted integration with production access, provide results of annual external penetration tests or equivalent third-party assessments within 30 days of completion.
   - Maintain and provide SCA and dependency-report artifacts for the past 12 months on request.

7) Incident Response and Forensics Support
   - If a security incident affects Company systems or data, Vendor must notify Company Security within 2 hours of detection and provide a preliminary incident report within 24 hours.
   - Vendor must preserve logs and forensic artifacts for at least 90 days and cooperate with Company forensic investigation requests.

Audit Rights and Evidence Requirements:
- Upon reasonable notice (typically 7 days), Company may request documentation and evidence that Vendor complies with the obligations in this addendum. Evidence may include:
  - SDLC policy excerpts and change log,
  - CI job definitions demonstrating SAST/SCA gates,
  - Recent dependency scan reports and mitigation tickets,
  - Signed release artifact manifests,
  - Pen test and remediation reports,
  - Employee training records for developers handling Company integrations.
- Company may also request a remote security review or agreed-upon-attestation (SOC2 Type II or equivalent) if Vendor refuses or cannot produce requested artifacts; costs allocation to be negotiated depending on findings.

Remedies for Non-Compliance:
- If Vendor fails to meet Critical remediation SLAs and no acceptable remediation plan exists, Company may suspend integrations, require temporary isolation of affected services, or terminate the agreement for material breach.
- Parties will seek a remediation-first approach; termination is a last resort after a 14-day cure period unless immediate risk requires earlier action.

Confidentiality and Data Handling:
- Nothing in this addendum alters obligations under the Data Processing Agreement. Security evidence exchanged under audit rights will be treated as Confidential Information.

Limitation of Liability and Insurance:
- Vendor is expected to maintain appropriate cyber liability insurance and provide certificate of insurance upon request. Insurance does not limit Vendor's obligations under this addendum.

Appendix A — Minimum Evidence Checklist (provided to Company upon request):
- Copy of SDLC policy and last 12 months of change logs.
- CI pipeline definitions showing SAST/SCA jobs and failure gates.
- Top 50 dependency scan results with open items and remediation tickets.
- Latest external penetration test with remediation status.
- Release manifest (artifact digests) for last three production releases.
- Incident response playbook excerpt and point-of-contact.
- Developer secure-coding training roster for staff touching Company integrations.

Appendix B — Example Remediation Timeline Table (illustrative):
- Critical (CVSS >=9.0): Acknowledge 6h, Plan 24h, Deploy 7 days (or compensate within 48h).
- High (7.0–8.9): Acknowledge 24h, Plan 72h, Deploy 30 days.

Negotiation Notes for Legal/Procurement Teams (advice for redlines):
- Push for objective SLAs (CVSS thresholds, calendar days) but allow for documented exceptions where multi-vendor stacks require coordination.
- Require an explicit remediation escalation path and executive contacts for unresolved Critical issues.
- Consider adding a clause for split-cost of urgent third-party fixes if Vendor refuses to remediate in good faith.

Execution:
This addendum may be executed electronically and incorporated into the Agreement between Company and Vendor as the "Secure Development & Patching Addendum".

Contact (Company Security):
- Security Program Manager: security-ops@redwood.ai
- Escalation (on-call): +1-555-0142 (for incident notifications)

Revision History:
- 2024-09-15: Initial draft.
- 2024-11-02: Added SLAs for acknowledgment windows and evidence checklist.

(End of template)
